short: Bundled phonetic-feature streams (M06) are new among non-acoustic recognizers but transfer acoustic-ASR clustering; test-set tuning inflates the gain; speaker-independent and silent claims untested.
position: The paper [@schultz2010modeling] changes the EMG acoustic model (M06): nine phonetic-feature streams whose models are bundled by decision trees, beside a phone stream. None of the 14 prior non-acoustic-signal recognizers bundles features (Appendix), but streams, tree clustering and a one-stream form of bundling come from acoustic ASR, as the authors state (§3.1–3.4): a transfer to EMG, standard. One bundled stream at a Gaussian count comparable to the phone system gains 10.6% relative (§3.4). The full gain, 47.15% to 31.49% WER, is optimistic: as the authors state (§3.3), weights and tree size were tuned on the test set. The "speaker-independent" result (M03) trains on the speakers it tests (§4). Usefulness for silent speech (§5) rests on audible scores, while the group's [concurrent] silent test with the same features gave above 80% WER for most of the 14 pilot speakers [@wand2009impact].
